themes_detail.label: Mysterious SPIT Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a near-zero 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 3,900% surge (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting either a sudden building code or construction compliance crisis in Fordham/University Heights, or a shift in how complaints are being categorized.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,900% increase)
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
245 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (129 alterations, 75 new buildings) suggest active construction activity
reporting_angles: Contact SPIT/DOB to identify which projects triggered complaints and what violations were found
Cross-reference with DOB permit data to see if spike correlates with specific alterations or new construction sites

themes_detail.label: Lead Hazard Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 5 last week compared to a baseline of 0.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 1,900% spike (z-score: 10.97)—raising urgent public health concerns in a district with older housing stock that may contain lead paint and plumbing.
evidence: 5 lead complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,900% increase)
Z-score of 10.97 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Community Board has standing request to Department of Health on 'public health issues,' suggesting prior awareness of health hazards
129 alteration permits filed in 90 days may include renovations disturbing lead-containing materials
reporting_angles: Interview DOH to learn what triggered the spike—were apartments tested, schools flagged, or remediation ordered?
Identify affected buildings/neighborhoods within Fordham/University Heights and speak to residents about children's health
Investigate whether lead testing and remediation services are accessible and funded for low-income families

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Assistance Requests Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints nearly tripled to 7 last week compared to a 2.0 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 250% increase (z-score: 3.78)—pointing to either a sudden influx of unhoused individuals or residents reporting inadequate services.
evidence: 7 Homeless Person Assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (250% increase)
Z-score of 3.78 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Community Board has standing budget request for 'senior center program requests,' suggesting vulnerability among older/at-risk populations
reporting_angles: Interview DHS and local street outreach teams to understand what caused the spike—new encampments, seasonal weather, service closures?
Visit communities identified in complaints to document conditions and speak with unhoused individuals about needs
Assess whether local shelters, drop-in centers, and supportive housing are adequately resourced

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Water Conservation complaints surged to 5 last week versus a 1.1 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—a 344% spike (z-score: 4.18)—suggesting possible water main breaks, DEP outreach, or acute conservation advisories affecting the district.
evidence: 5 Water Conservation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% increase)
Z-score of 4.18 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Heat/Hot Water remains top complaint category (5,305 over 90 days), suggesting aging building infrastructure vulnerable to water system disruptions
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if water main breaks, construction, or emergency conservation orders triggered complaints
Check whether boil water advisories or service disruptions affected residential or institutional customers
Assess infrastructure aging and repair schedules in Fordham/University Heights

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Unexpectedly Decline
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints dropped 31% this week to 166 versus a 241.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: -5.46)—a counterintuitive decline that may signal either improved conditions, underreporting, or a shift in complaint methodology.
evidence: 166 residential noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 241.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (31% decrease)
Z-score of -5.46 indicates statistically significant anomaly (departure from norm)
Noise remains 2nd-largest complaint category overall (2,956 over 90 days), suggesting continued resident concern
reporting_angles: Investigate whether 311 system changes, school closures, or weather patterns explain the dip
Confirm whether this is seasonal or a genuine improvement before reporting as positive story
